title: Article 81 — Composition of the House of the People

content.overview: Article 81 provides for the composition of the House of the People (Lok Sabha): not more than 530 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the States, and not more than 20 members to represent the Union territories. Seats are allocated to States in such manner that the ratio between seats and population is, so far as practicable, the same for each State. Article 82 deals with readjustment after each census (currently frozen in material respects until after the first census post-2026).
content.glance: Lok Sabha: ≤530 from States (direct election) + ≤20 from UTs. Population-proportionate allocation. Readjustment: Art 82 (freeze until post-2026 census).
content.study:
Article 81:

Subject to Article 331 (Anglo-Indian nomination — historically; now largely spent after 104th Amendment), the House of the People consists of—
(a) not more than 530 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the States; and
(b) not more than 20 members to represent the Union territories, chosen in such manner as Parliament may by law provide.

For States: allocation of seats and division into territorial constituencies is such that the ratio between the number of seats and population is, so far as practicable, the same throughout.

Article 82: readjustment after each census. Delimitation and related freeze provisions (including amendments linked to the 42nd/84th Amendment line) have deferred fresh readjustment of seats among States until after the first census taken after 2026.

Examination: max 530 + max 20; direct election; population ratio; link Art 82 and the post-2026 census freeze.

sections.heading: Composition
sections.body:
- ≤530 members from States (direct election from territorial constituencies).
- ≤20 members representing Union territories (manner prescribed by Parliament).
- Allocation among States: population-proportionate so far as practicable.

sections.heading: Readjustment (Article 82 link)
sections.body: Article 82 requires readjustment of allocation of seats and division of constituencies after each census. Material freeze provisions defer inter-State seat reallocation until after the first census following 2026.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Explain the composition of the House of the People under Article 81.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 81, the House of the People consists of not more than 530 members chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies in the States, and not more than 20 members to represent the Union territories (chosen as Parliament may by law provide). Seats are allocated to States so that the ratio of seats to population is, so far as practicable, the same for each State. Readjustment after each census is governed by Article 82; inter-State seat reallocation is currently deferred until after the first census post-2026.
